svg.text: The verification bundle, and its blind spots
One command runs everything below and refuses to pass on a warning. This is the machine half of “agents produce, machines verify,
humans decide”. Each row states the claim the check earns and, beside it, the claim it does not — because a bundle that reports only green
teaches its reader to trust it for things it never examined.
the bridge code behaves as its tests describe
the tests were written by the same author as the code
every skill parses and carries the AIRL metadata
no skill has been run against a task and scored
every sealed planning file is byte-identical to the
a sealed document can still be wrong
identifiers resolve, references are bidirectional, the DAG
feasibility of the work itself is not modelled
every generated index matches its directory
nothing about the content of what is indexed
numbers written in prose match the repository
only the numbers that were registered as rules
no document claims a state the repository has outgrown
a claim can be current and still false
the queue follows the sealed dependencies and the
whether a package that is ready is worth starting
every path, command and count in AGENTS.md
whether the guidance it gives is good advice
every figure is byte-identical to what its generator
whether a figure argues its point
no glyph in any figure overflows its box, re-measured
every external claim has a type, a source and a retrieval
whether the source actually says it
every assimilated mechanism names its upstream, its
licence and what it may never decide
whether the mechanism was worth taking; its
every vault link resolves, every projected page names
its source, every tag is in the vocabulary
whether any note in it is worth reading
each package states its true prerequisite closure and
whether the package is well designed
every package carries a test procedure and an
whether the cases in them are the right cases
Why it holds: the bundle is not allowed to be optional
Everything here is internal consistency. The bundle can confirm that this repository says the same thing everywhere, that its plan is
well-formed and that its evidence verifies — and all of that would still hold for a corpus describing a system that does not work.
External truth enters through exactly two doors: reference verification against Crossref, OpenAlex and arXiv, and the benchmarks
named in the adoption matrix, none of which has been run.
